title: A save comes back as the same city: 44 excused fields become 4, each named with its owner, its file and its fix — and two of them are disproved as excuses by a test that puts them back by hand

verified.REVERT PROOF, LcnStateReconciler._congru: test_a_repair_may_never_hand_a_system_a_shape_it_cannot_read RED (3 assertions) AND 2 x `Invalid access to property or key 'priority'` engine errors in the suite log, which tools/scan_errors.py grades
verified.gap probe (tests/save/save_gaps.gd): putting [P06]'s standing forces and [P08]'s approach paths back by hand closes BOTH fields outright and leaves nothing else behind — the gap list is the whole of it, measured rather than asserted
verified.tools/determinism.sh: DETERMINISM OK — smoke IDENTICAL sha256 cb03fec35508f687, determinism IDENTICAL sha256 a6ba7f017dae1a50. File unchanged (git status tools/ shows only another agent's untracked ui_tour*.gd)
verified.two doors, measured in tests/meta/test_s: Sim.deserialize loses 8 leaves; LcnSaveManager.apply_world loses 40, i.e. 32 MORE — it re-implements the loader without the repair pass

open: [P24] game/ui/meta/save_manager.gd:apply_world() re-implements Sim.deserialize() minus the reconciler, and its own class comment already says 'nothing here re-implements any of that'. The body becomes `return bool(Sim.deserialize(world)["ok"])` and 32 fields stop being lost on the player's door. This part may not write in game/ui/**; tests/meta/test_save_roundtrip.gd measures the delta on every run so it cannot go quiet.

[P06] game/sim/society/ — SocietyPressures has serialize() and no inverse, and SocietySystem.deserialize() recomputes the standing forces instead of reading them back. Because _sample() polls the council AFTER rebuilding the pressures, a recompute at load time sees one sample more of council state than the save did and four grievance forces stand that were not standing. Fix: an inverse over keys/labels/texts/rates/meters + _ceiling, called from deserialize().

[P08] game/sim/threat/threat_vector.gd — to_dict() writes `path.size()` as `cells` and never `path`, so the approach corridor the night was planned around is not in the save at all and a resumed siege walks a lane of length zero. Two lines: write `path` in to_dict(), read it in from_dict().

[P22] game/narrative/narrative_system.gd:950 — deserialize() rebuilds a waiting card only when `by_id` knows its id, and chapter beats are raised from the chapter table rather than from game/content/events/**. Measured: `the_column_stopped` is in the save, is not among by_id's 26 ids, and is dropped. Every chapter beat waiting on the player dies in a load.

[P10] game/sim/research/ — the pacing window is a rolling measurement over recent ticks that deserialize() does not carry, so a reloaded director re-derives it from the single instant it woke up in (threat level 25% -> 20%).

INTEGRATOR / architecture: `Sim.serialize()` is a REPORT before it is a save format. Every part snaps its floats on the way out (snappedf(hope_value, 0.001), morale to 0.01), so a save cannot carry more than three decimals, a reload starts up to half a grain off, and an integrator amplifies that into a different death by old age 400 ticks later. Byte-identical AT REST is achievable and is achieved; tick-for-tick replay across a save is NOT, and will not be until the save carries unrounded floats. Measured: one tick after a load nothing has moved further than 0.01; four hundred ticks after one, citizens' morale is 1.2 apart and one person has died in one city and not the other. Deciding whether §0.4's 'non-negotiable' covers a reload is an architecture call, not a save-layer one.

The 'nine failures' in the brief were partly a MEASUREMENT ARTEFACT and the artefact is now fixed: user://saves/ and game/core/settings.cfg are one path per MACHINE, not per process, and four agents on four cores each wrote test_roundtrip.lcn, rotated autosave_1..3 and rewrote settings.cfg over each other. The reported '44 fields differ, including $.seed, all six RNG streams and $.systems.grid.hash' was two different cities being compared; every one of those fields round-trips perfectly. tests/save/save_slots.gd gives every slot this process's id and holds a machine-wide lock for the suites that cannot be namespaced.

NOT VERIFIED BY ME: the full tools/check.sh (perf, visual, reachability). game/core/harness.gd, game/boot.gd and game/sim/climate/ were being edited by other agents throughout this session — the tree failed to parse twice mid-run — so perf and any windowed stage measured now would be measuring them, not me. The integrator measures perf.
